target_node.label: Glowworm Optical Side-Channel Acoustic Recovery Attack
target_node.precondition: Target Raspberry Pi (3 B+ or 4 B through 2021-08-09) supplies power directly to connected audio speakers playing sound; optical line-of-sight to the power indicator LED exists with an electro-optical sensor and telescope.
target_node.postcondition: Attacker remotely reconstructs and eavesdrops on speech and acoustic signals output by speakers through optical fluctuations in power LED intensity.

source_evidence.description: Raspberry Pi OS through 5.10 has the raspberry default password for the pi account. If not changed, attackers can gain administrator privileges.

Raspberry Pi 3 B+ and 4 B devices through 2021-08-09, in certain specific use cases in which the device supplies power to audio-output equipment, allow remote attackers to recover speech signals from an LED on the device, via a telescope and an electro-optical sensor, aka a "Glowworm" attack. We assume that the Raspberry Pi supplies power to some speakers. The power indicator LED of the Raspberry Pi is connected directly to the power line, as a result, the intensity of a device's power indicator LED is correlative to the power consumption. The sound played by the speakers affects the Raspberry Pi's power consumption and as a result is also correlative to the light intensity of the LED. By analyzing measurements obtained from an electro-optical sensor directed at the power indicator LED of the Raspberry Pi, we can recover the sound played by the speakers.

edge.label: Arbitrary command execution allows attacker to deploy audio playback commands through connected equipment, facilitating optical eavesdropping via the Glowworm attack.

source_node.label: Oculus Browser Remote HTML Injection and UI Spoofing
source_node.precondition: Target user visits a malicious remote web page using Oculus Browser (versions 5.2.7 through 5.7.11).
source_node.postcondition: Attacker spoofs browser UI elements and achieves unprivileged local code execution within the Oculus Browser process context.

target_node.label: Oculus Desktop OVRRedir.exe Hard Link Arbitrary File Write Privilege Escalation
target_node.precondition: Attacker has local unprivileged code execution on a Windows host running Oculus Desktop before 1.44.0.32849 with a privileged OVRRedir.exe process.
target_node.postcondition: Attacker writes to arbitrary system files via hard-linked log files, escalating privileges to NT AUTHORITY\SYSTEM.

source_evidence.description: A remote web page could inject arbitrary HTML code into the Oculus Browser UI, allowing an attacker to spoof UI and potentially execute code. This affects the Oculus Browser starting from version 5.2.7 until 5.7.11.

Writing to an unprivileged file from a privileged OVRRedir.exe process in Oculus Desktop before 1.44.0.32849 on Windows allows local users to write to arbitrary files and consequently gain privileges via vectors involving a hard link to a log file.

target_node.precondition: Attacker has local unprivileged process execution on a Windows host running Oculus Desktop (versions after 1.39 and prior to 31.1.0.67.507) with OVRServiceLauncher.exe.
target_node.postcondition: Attacker acquires a leaked privileged process handle, leading to local privilege escalation to NT AUTHORITY\SYSTEM.

source_evidence.description: A remote web page could inject arbitrary HTML code into the Oculus Browser UI, allowing an attacker to spoof UI and potentially execute code. This affects the Oculus Browser starting from version 5.2.7 until 5.7.11.

Due to a bug with management of handles in OVRServiceLauncher.exe, an attacker could expose a privileged process handle to an unprivileged process, leading to local privilege escalation. This issue affects Oculus Desktop versions after 1.39 and prior to 31.1.0.67.507.
